concepts.label: resource
concepts.gloss: A resource is an identifiable managed entity in the network or service environment whose state, behavior, and operational observations can be monitored or managed.
concepts.example: node-14 is a managed network node, while ctr-app-node14 is a managed application container hosted on that node.

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: An event is a discrete, time-associated notification reporting that something occurred or a state changed on a particular managed resource, without necessarily implying abnormality.
concepts.example: trap-cpu-node14-t0 is a notification emitted for node-14 at time t0 after a CPU-related state change was observed.

concepts.label: anomaly
concepts.gloss: An anomaly is a detected deviation of a resource's observed behavior or state from an expected baseline or pattern.
concepts.example: cpu-node14-rising represents detection that CPU utilization on node-14 is rising abnormally relative to its expected behavior.

concepts.label: symptom
concepts.gloss: A symptom is an observable manifestation or indicator through which an anomaly becomes evident.
concepts.example: symptom-1 may record repeated high-CPU measurements as the manifestation of the cpu-node14-rising anomaly.

concepts.label: fault
concepts.gloss: A fault is an occurrence of an erroneous or failed condition in a managed resource that can impair its intended operation.
concepts.example: fault-1 records that a CPU scheduling component on node-14 entered a failed condition and could no longer provide normal processing capacity.

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: An alarm is a managed indication of an abnormal resource condition that remains operationally relevant until it is cleared or otherwise changes state.
concepts.example: alarm-1 is raised on node-14 when sustained CPU saturation crosses an alarm threshold and remains active until utilization recovers.

concepts.label: problem
concepts.gloss: A problem is a diagnostic interpretation that explains one or more observed fault occurrences in terms of an underlying operational issue.
concepts.example: problem-1 diagnoses resource exhaustion as the issue explaining fault-1 on node-14.

concepts.label: cause
concepts.gloss: A cause is the identified causal factor that produced or sustains a diagnosed problem.
concepts.example: cause-1 identifies an unbounded workload in ctr-app-node14 as the root cause of problem-1.

concepts.label: incident
concepts.gloss: An incident is a correlation and management grouping that collects related anomalies into one operational case for coordinated investigation or response.
concepts.example: incident-1 groups cpu-node14-rising with related latency and container-resource anomalies observed during the same service-impacting episode.

concepts.label: concern-score
concepts.gloss: A concern-score is a numeric annotation expressing how operationally concerning or worthy of attention an anomaly is, independently of certainty that the anomaly was detected correctly.
concepts.example: The cpu-node14-rising anomaly receives concern-score 0.9 because its likely operational impact is high.

concepts.label: confidence-score
concepts.gloss: A confidence-score is a numeric annotation expressing the assessed certainty that an identified anomaly is valid or correctly characterized, independently of its operational importance.
concepts.example: The cpu-node14-rising anomaly receives confidence-score 0.7 because the detector has moderately strong evidence that the rise is genuinely anomalous.
